newsitem.title: CHINA: Most Chinese choose savings despite lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Most Chinese choose savings despite lower rates.

text.p: Most Chinese still consider bank deposits their primary investment tool despite two interest rate cuts last year, the Economic Daily said on Friday.
A recent survey by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, found that 52.7 percent of Chinese in major cities prefer to deposit their money rather than spend it, it said.
China cut interest rates last May and again in August to ease credit as prices fell. The August cut trimmed bank deposit rates by an average of 1.5 percentage points.
The proportion of short-term current deposits increased while long-term fixed deposits declined because of the interest rate cuts, the survey said.
In the August cut, the central bank trimmed interest rates on one-year deposits by 1.71 percentage points while the rate on three-year savings fell by 2.52 percentage points.
The proportion of current deposits among total new bank deposits surged to 55.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, compared with 5.2 percent in the first quarter, it said.
China's total private deposits in both urban and rural areas reached 3,852 billion yuan ($464 billion) at the end of 1996, up 29.9 percent from end-1995.
